name: OCT4 + SOX2 + KLF4
notes: High rejuvenation signal but requires tight expression control and strong tumor surveillance

name: OCT4 + SOX2 + KLF4 + MYC
notes: Useful benchmark but too risky for direct in-vivo rejuvenation because of MYC and pluripotency drift

name: OCT4
notes: Powerful cell-state driver but high identity-loss risk when used alone

name: SOX2
notes: Potentially useful in neural contexts but cancer and fate-shift risks need gating

name: KLF4
mechanism: Reprogramming factor with context-dependent proliferation effects
notes: Safer than MYC in many settings but still needs transient expression control

name: MYC
notes: Usually a negative-control risk flag for rejuvenation programs

name: SIRT6
mechanism: DNA repair chromatin and metabolic stress regulator
notes: Good low-risk adjunct candidate rather than full reprogramming driver

name: TET2
mechanism: DNA demethylation and hematopoietic epigenetic regulation
notes: Interesting for epigenetic age but clonal hematopoiesis risk makes context critical

name: LIN28A
notes: Potential regeneration enhancer but identity and tumor risks need careful screens

name: FOXO3
mechanism: Stress resistance and longevity-associated transcription factor
notes: More likely a safety-supporting network modulator than a rejuvenation switch
